title: RL fine-tune trains each proof only at loop counts at or above the depth that found it
description: Pretraining, the sampling schedule (8 attempts per target at each of 1, 2, 4 and 8 loops per round), replay, weighting, optimizer and round rule are the incumbent's. Only which loop counts a proof is fine-tuned at changes. rl() records for every accepted proof the shallowest loop count among the oracle calls that returned it (its discovery depth; replayed pretraining records count as depth 1). finetune() draws each step's loop count n from TRAIN_LOOPS = 1..8 first (a new model.train_loops attribute pins the forward to that n), then draws the 128-record batch with replacement from the records whose discovery depth is <= n, weighting record i by 1 / P(n >= depth_i) (1, 8/7, 8/5 and 8 for depths 1, 2, 4, 8) so every record's expected exposure per round equals the incumbent's unfiltered epochs. So a proof found only at 8 loops is trained only in 8-loop batches, a proof found at 1 loop (and all replay) in every batch. rl() also returns rl_records_by_depth, the per-round count of RL records at each discovery depth. No change to speed: same sampling, same 600 steps.
hypothesis: In run 500 the pretrained model's accuracy on RL targets rose 3.6x from 1 to 8 loops (0.024, 0.059, 0.081, 0.088 at 1, 2, 4, 8) and the fine-tune then flattened it: by round 5 it was 0.708, 0.752, 0.763, 0.763. The incumbent fine-tunes every proof at a random loop count 1..8, so the one-pass core is asked to reproduce the proofs only deep passes found; the cheapest shared solution is a one-shot core whose later passes are near-identity (pretraining already lands there: val loss within 0.002 across 1-8 loops), and that is what makes 8 loops no better than 4. Training a proof only at loop counts >= its discovery depth removes that pressure: the 8-loop forward still trains on every proof, the 1-loop forward only on proofs it already produces, so the core is free to be a partial step that needs iterating for hard proofs, as in Geiping et al. 2025 where shallow recurrences are rarely demanded. 501 showed the RL fine-tune can reshape the depth profile in 3000 steps (2-loop accuracy fell from 0.46 to 0.30 when only 8 loops were trained), so the effect should be visible within RL_SECS. Discovery depth is noisy at k=8 (a proof found at 8 and missed at 1 may be luck), which only softens the curriculum. Risks: the one-shot constraint was never binding (capacity, not depth, limits the trunk; the spike's long-dev ceiling of 16.8% at any depth suggests this) and nothing changes; or with-replacement weighted batches noisier than epochs cost a little.
expected_delta: metric at 8 loops 670-700 (3-seed mean; +0 to +25 over 675), metric_diag at 2 loops 590-650 (proofs found at 4 or 8 loops are no longer trained at 2), so metric minus diag widens from 500's +18 to at least +35. Mechanism check in rl_rounds: in the last round, sample_acc at level 1 at most 0.65 against 500's 0.708 while level 8 stays at or above 0.76, i.e. the 1-vs-8 gap grows from 0.055 to at least 0.10. RL rounds 5 per seed as in 500 (no speed change); cumulative RL targets solved 1120-1200 (500: 1149). rl_records_by_depth: depth-1 records a growing majority across rounds, depth-8-only records 5-15% of RL records in round 1 falling later. If metric is within noise of 675 and the 1-vs-8 RL gap did not widen, the one-pass constraint was not what limits depth. Discard unless mean metric > 675.

arch.type: looped gpt: 1 entry + 2 shared core x n + 1 exit Peri-LN blocks, LayerNorm(state)+entry re-injection per loop

optimizer.name: muon (polar express) on block matrices and head + adamw on the rest

config.init: orthogonal on block matrices, fork default elsewhere

rl.rounds: until another round would not fit in RL_SECS
rl.ft_optimizer: adamw, warmup 50 then cosine to lr/10
rl.ft_loops: uniform over 1..8 per step, drawn before the batch
rl.ft_depth_rule: record eligible at loop count n iff its discovery depth <= n; discovery depth = shallowest sampling loop count that returned the proof, replay = 1
rl.ft_batch_sampling: 128 records with replacement from the eligible set, weight 1 / P(n >= depth): 1, 8/7, 8/5, 8 for depths 1, 2, 4, 8
rl.loss: next-token CE on the last loop's output

rl.oracle: Lean AND nd_verify accepted samples of the model's own attempts

eval.metric: dev-transfer theorems solved at L_true >= 7 with KNOB at EVAL_LEVEL
